passage: Every second Saturday, our school volunteer group visits the Sunshine Home, where twenty elderly people live. Last weekend I went there for the first time. Grandma Li held my hand with a big smile, and I felt warm at once. We cleaned the windows and swept the floor. My friend Amy played the violin, and everyone clapped. I read a story to Grandpa Wang because his eyes were weak. He said, "Your voice is like my granddaughter's. Thank you, child." At lunch, we made dumplings together. Grandma Li's hands were slow but her smile was bright. When we left, I felt the happiest I had been all month. I learned that helping others is really a gift we give to ourselves.
q: How often does the volunteer group visit the Sunshine Home?
explain: 开头说 "Every second Saturday, our school volunteer group visits the Sunshine Home"，即每两周的周六去一次。

passage: Sometimes we do not need to speak - our body speaks for us. When you meet a friend, you smile. When you agree, you nod. When a ball comes at you, you shout "Watch out!" with open hands more than with words. This is body language. Our face is a small stage. It shows if we are happy, tired, worried or angry. A real smile travels across countries, and even babies understand it. Our hands are busy actors. We use them to point, to count, to say hello or goodbye. A warm handshake starts a friendship. A gentle pat on the shoulder says, "You did a good job." Body language is the first language we ever learn. We use it long before we speak. And even when we grow up, it never stops talking for us.
q: According to the passage, what is body language?
options: A foreign language we study at school
The way our body communicates without words
A kind of sign used only by deaf people
explain: 文章说不开口时身体替我们说话，如微笑、点头，"This is body language"，即用身体而非言语交流。

passage: My grandma is 78. Her hands are thin and wrinkled, but they can do magic. She is a master of paper-cutting. She learned the skill at eight from her mother. At first she only cut simple shapes - a flower, a star, a fish. By fifteen, she could cut a dragon with every scale clear. Every Spring Festival, our neighbours come to ask her for window flowers. Last winter, Grandma taught me. She gave me a soft red paper and small scissors. "Hold the paper loosely and move the scissors slowly. Feel the paper like a friend," she said. My first rabbit had a broken ear; my second rabbit had three legs. Grandma laughed, but she was patient. By my tenth try, my rabbit looked like a rabbit at last! Grandma says, "A skill is like a seed. If nobody plants it, it dies."
q: At what age did Grandma learn paper-cutting?
explain: "She learned the skill at eight from her mother."

passage: Last Christmas, my uncle gave me an unusual present - a small white robot called Buddy. Buddy is only 30 centimetres tall but he can do many things. In the morning, Buddy wakes me up with a soft song, tells me the weather and reads the news in English. While I brush my teeth, he moves around my bed and picks up dirty socks. When I do homework, Buddy sits quietly on my desk. If I ask a hard math question, his eyes turn blue and he gives a clear answer. Sometimes he even makes a small joke. But Buddy is not perfect. He does not like water - one rainy day he ran outside by mistake, and I had to dry him for an hour. He also has a weak battery, so he must rest for two hours every afternoon. I know Buddy is just a machine, but I enjoy his company.
q: How tall is Buddy?
explain: "Buddy is only 30 centimetres tall."

passage: Last summer my family joined a five-day nature trip to Sanjiangyuan in Qinghai - the source of the Yangtze, Yellow and Lancang rivers. Sanjiangyuan is home to many rare animals - snow leopards, Tibetan antelopes, black-necked cranes and brown bears. Because of hunting and climate change, their numbers dropped sharply in the last century. Today, things are changing. Since 2000, the Chinese government has set up large reserves. Over 3,000 rangers ride horses day and night to protect the animals. The Tibetan antelope population went from 20,000 in the 1990s to over 70,000 today. On the third morning, our guide pointed to a hill. Far away, a group of Tibetan antelopes were running in the sunshine. Nobody spoke. We just watched quietly.
q: What is Sanjiangyuan the source of?
options: The Yangtze, Yellow and Lancang rivers
explain: "the source of the Yangtze, Yellow and Lancang rivers."

passage: When I was six, my grandfather gave me a small flower pot and a few tomato seeds. That was my first garden. He told me three secrets. First, plants need good soil - not too dry and not too wet. Second, plants love sunlight, so put the pot where the morning sun can reach. Third, plants are like children - they need love and patience. I watered the seeds every day and checked them every hour. On the seventh morning, I saw two tiny green leaves! I shouted so loud that the whole family came running. Three months later, I had ten shining red tomatoes. Mum made a salad, and we all ate the tomatoes I had grown. It tasted like sunshine. I am fourteen now. I have a larger garden on our balcony - lettuce, chilli peppers, mint and even a small lemon tree.
q: What did the grandfather give the writer at the age of six?
options: A flower pot and a few tomato seeds
explain: "my grandfather gave me a small flower pot and a few tomato seeds."
